identity.name: South Seas Mandate
alt_names: Mandated Territory of the South Sea Islands

land.text: 'the Micronesian islands north of the equator, formerly part of German New Guinea': the Marianas, Carolines, Marshall Islands and Palau

predecessors.note: Japan 'seized the Marianas, Carolines, Marshall Islands and Palau groups by October 1914'; the page dates the mandate to 1920 (infobox 1920-1947) without a day. December 1920 follows the Australian mandate (17 December 1920).

land.text: the same islands: 'The League of Nations mandate was formally revoked by the United Nations on 18 July 1947'; the United States became responsible 'under a trusteeship that established the Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands'

successors.note: Guam, held by the United States, was never part of the mandate.

capitals.name: Truk (Chuuk)
capitals.note: 'The Civil Affairs Bureau was initially based in Truk'.

capitals.name: Koror
capitals.note: 'moved to Koror in the Palau islands in 1921'; the Nan'yō-chō (South Seas Government) of March 1932 sat there on the page's account of the bureau (page silent on the 1932 seat). Under US occupation from 1944 to 1945 the islands were not governed from Koror.

correction.text: 'the Micronesian islands north of the equator' - the Marianas (except Guam), Carolines, Marshall Islands and Palau, in the six districts of Saipan, Palau, Yap, Truk, Ponape and Jaluit

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 7 grid cells (about 1,800 km2); the page gives no area, and the German New Guinea page's table gives the Carolines about 2,150 km2, Palau 466, Marianas 461 and Marshalls 181 (3,258 km2 together). The page gives no exclusion of Guam in words; Guam was American and is not in this shape. The shape holds to 1947; the US occupation of 1944 to 1947 is drawn by occupation events, not by a smaller shape.

region.text: the Micronesian islands north of the equator, formerly part of German New Guinea

ledger.note: 1920: Japan receives the League of Nations mandate for the South Seas Islands: 'a League of Nations mandate given to the Empire of Japan by the League of Nations following World War I' (infobox 'Class C League of Nations mandate of Japan (1920-1947)'). Japan had 'seized the Marianas, Carolines, Marshall Islands and Palau groups by October 1914'. The page gives no day; December 1920 is the researcher's reading.
1921: the Civil Affairs Bureau, 'initially based in Truk', 'moved to Koror in the Palau islands in 1921'.

1932: the South Seas Government (Nan'yō-chō) is set up: 'The establishment of the South Seas Government or Nan'yō-chō in March 1932 finally put the government of the islands under a purely civilian administration.' Same state, same colour (rule 2).

region.text: the Marshall Islands: Majuro, Kwajalein and Eniwetok atolls, the islands the Americans chose to invade

ledger.note: 1944: the Marshall Islands campaign opens (31 January 1944): the Majuro landing 'marked the beginning of Operation Flintlock, the invasion of Kwajalein'.
1944: the Marshall Islands campaign ends in February: Kwajalein was captured on 7 February and the whole of Eniwetok atoll 'by 23 February'; 'This marked an end to the Marshall Islands campaign.'

region.text: the Marshall Islands, taken by the United States in the Marshall Islands campaign

ledger.note: 1944: the United States holds the Marshall Islands from February 1944. The page dates the captures of Kwajalein (7 February) and Eniwetok (23 February); Jaluit, Maloelap, Wotje and Mili, where Japanese forces were dispersed, are not said to have fallen, so the whole group is the researcher's reading at cell level.

region.text: the Mariana Islands (Saipan, Tinian) of the mandate; Guam was American territory

ledger.note: 1944: the Mariana Islands campaign opens: 'Battle of Saipan, 15 June - 9 July 1944'; Tinian 24 July to 1 August 1944.

region.text: the Mariana Islands of the mandate

ledger.note: 1944: the Marianas are secured: 'After heavy fighting, Saipan was secured in July and Guam and Tinian in August 1944.'

region.text: the Mariana Islands of the mandate

ledger.note: 1944: the United States holds the Northern Mariana Islands from August 1944 ('Saipan was secured in July and Guam and Tinian in August 1944'); the smaller islands to the north are not dated on the page.

region.text: Peleliu and Angaur in the Palau Islands (below the grid)

ledger.note: 1944: the Palau campaign opens: 'Battle of Peleliu, 15 September - 27 November 1944'; Angaur 17 September to 22 October 1944.
1944: Peleliu and Angaur are secured: 'both islands were finally secured by U.S. forces in November 1944'; Koror 'was bypassed altogether, only to surrender in August 1945'.

region.text: the Palau Islands and the Caroline Islands (Chuuk, Yap, Pohnpei, Kosrae), bypassed in 1944

ledger.note: 1945: the bypassed islands pass to American occupation at Japan's capitulation: the Palau page says the Koror garrison 'was bypassed altogether, only to surrender in August 1945 with the Japan's capitulation'; the same is the researcher's reading for Truk, Yap, Pohnpei and Kosrae (the page is silent on them). The Japanese mandate government ceases to rule.
1947: the American occupation of the Marshall Islands ends as the trusteeship begins (18 July 1947).

region.text: the Mariana Islands of the mandate

ledger.note: 1947: the American occupation of the Mariana Islands of the mandate ends as the trusteeship begins (18 July 1947).

region.text: the Palau Islands and the Caroline Islands

ledger.note: 1947: the American occupation of the Palau Islands and the Caroline Islands ends as the trusteeship begins (18 July 1947).
1947: the mandate is revoked. 'The League of Nations mandate was formally revoked by the United Nations on 18 July 1947'; the islands become the United States' Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands.

wars.name: Gilbert and Marshall Islands campaign
wars.outcome: Majuro and Kwajalein (from 31 January 1944; Kwajalein captured 7 February) and Eniwetok (17 to 23 February 1944): 'This marked an end to the Marshall Islands campaign.' The Gilbert Islands (Tarawa, 20 to 23 November 1943) were British, not part of the mandate.
wars.note: The page does not say the other atolls were bypassed; the page says Japanese forces were dispersed to Maloelap, Wotje, Jaluit and Mili.

wars.name: Mariana and Palau Islands campaign
wars.outcome: Saipan 15 June to 9 July, Tinian 24 July to 1 August, Guam 21 July to 10 August (American territory, retaken); Peleliu 15 September to 27 November, Angaur 17 September to 22 October 1944. Koror was bypassed and surrendered in August 1945.

certainty.note: Islands: the border is the coast and the mandate's limit at the equator; Guam's exclusion is a fact of American sovereignty. Control during the Pacific War shifts by atoll and is dated only for the campaign islands.

sources.title: German New Guinea
sources.note: The 1914 Japanese seizure and the mandate's origin in German Micronesia (cited by the german-new-guinea dossier).

sources.title: Gilbert and Marshall Islands campaign
sources.note: Marshall Islands campaign: Majuro/Kwajalein 31 January 1944, Kwajalein 7 February, Eniwetok 17 to 23 February; Tarawa 20-23 November 1943.

sources.title: Mariana and Palau Islands campaign
sources.note: Saipan 15 June to 9 July, Tinian, Guam, Peleliu and Angaur 1944; Koror bypassed, surrender August 1945.

sources.title: South Seas Mandate
sources.note: Mandate 1920-1947, six districts (April 1922), Koror from 1921, Nan'yō-chō March 1932, League withdrawal 1933-35, mandate revoked 18 July 1947, 1939 population.

notes:
Written by oc-02-x. Pages used: South Seas Mandate, Gilbert and Marshall Islands campaign, Mariana and Palau Islands campaign, German New Guinea (for the 1914 seizure and the 1920 handover).
MODEL. A colony dossier (rule 2: a dependency ruled from elsewhere) of Japan's family, written because Cliopatria has no Mandate. empire-of-japan (jk-01) already draws the same islands from 1920 as 'gain german-empire' and 'loss united-states-of-america 1945'; the rendering should let this dossier carry the land and treat Japan as its metropole (the vassal tint), and the Japan dossier's 1914 and 1920 events should read counterpart german-new-guinea. The Micronesian islands before 1920 belong to german-new-guinea (to 1920-12, hatched Japanese from September 1914). Seven grid cells in all.
The Pacific War: the first campaign of each group opens a contest with the United States and an American occupation (hatching) follows; the mandate legally lasts to 18 July 1947. The Truk, Yap, Pohnpei and Kosrae garrisons were bypassed; no page opened dates their surrender (confidence 1 event). Not on the pages: 17 December 1920, the 1922 mandate agreement, an area, the post-1932 seat of the Nan'yō-chō. Japan 'gave notice of withdrawal from the League of Nations' in 1933, effective two years later (1935); the mandate continued; the terms 'required Japan not to fortify the islands' (the 1930s build-up is on the page). Population: 129,104 in the December 1939 census.
